title: Approximants de Padé et mesures effectives d'irrationalité
status: read, 21 September 2026 (scan on the Desktop, 28Rhin_Sm_Paris_1987.pdf; local copy literature/sources/rhin-1987-pade-irrationality.pdf, untracked)
notes: Séminaire de Théorie des Nombres, Paris 1985-86, Progress in Mathematics 71, Birkhäuser, 1987, pp. 155-164. THE PROPOSITION, p. 160: for integers u_0, u_1, u_2 with H = max(|u_1|, |u_2|) >= 2, the form Lambda = u_0 + u_1 log 2 + u_2 log 3 satisfies (7) |Lambda| >= H^(-13.3), with no further constant and for every H >= 2; and (8) |Lambda| >= H^(-7.616) for H >= H_0, H_0 effectively computable but not given. The proof of (7) uses the best simultaneous approximations q log 2 - p_1, q log 3 - p_2 for q < 7.32 * 10^12 (Dubois and Toffin, Macsyma); Baker's method gives 2^50 in place of 13.3. So the laboratory's form exp(-13.3 (0.46057 + log K)) is not Rhin's statement but Simons-de Weger 2005 Lemma 12, Rhin's (7) at H = K + L expressed through the odd count K with log delta = 0.46057; with H taken as the cycle length itself the bound is H^(-13.3), a factor delta^13.3 = 457 stronger, and that is the form negative_m_cycles uses. Paper A's Corollary 4.11 already states the strong form L^(-13.3) <= Lambda and notes 2 e^6.1256 < 915 for the weak one. The rest of the paper: effective irrationality measures by Padé-type integrals, mu(log 2) = 4.0765 with the polynomial of the appendix, mu(pi/sqrt 3) = 4.97, mu(sqrt 3 log(2+sqrt 3)) = 17.207; Théorème 3 (Rhin-Toffin) for several logarithms. The transcendence estimate remains an external theorem, not a Lean proof.
